title: REMOP: REmote-Memory-aware OPerator Optimization
event_hint: REMOP framework for remote-memory-aware database operator optimization
problem: Classical disk-spilling operator heuristics minimize I/O volume but can trigger excessive transfer rounds under remote memory where each round incurs fixed RTT, making total latency sensitive to round count
mechanism: Transfer-round-aware intra-operator buffer partitioning strategies; derives operator-specific input/output buffer splits for blocked nested-loop join, external merge sort, and external hash join to minimize total latency L = D/BW + C*RTT

evidence.claim: REMOP reduces transfer rounds by up to 97% and operator runtime by up to 48% on spill-heavy microbenchmarks
evidence.condition: BNLJ single-operator query, selectivity f=1/256K, memory budget M=4K pages, two-node compute-memory testbed

evidence.claim: REMOP reduces BNLJ runtime by 48.7% and transfer rounds by 97.1% at L-optimal buffer settings
evidence.condition: BNLJ with (rin=0.4, pR=0.6), selectivity f=1/256K, M=4K pages

evidence.claim: REMOP lowers average runtime of spilling TPC-H queries by 22.7%
evidence.condition: TPC-H spilling queries, two-node compute-memory testbed

evidence.claim: REMOP lowers average runtime of spilling TPC-DS queries by 26.4%
evidence.condition: TPC-DS spilling queries, two-node compute-memory testbed

evidence.claim: REMOP achieves gains up to 51% under higher remote-memory latency

evaluation_context: Two-node compute-memory testbed; DuckDB implementation; TCP-based REMON and RDMA-based Infiniswap backends evaluated; microbenchmarks for BNLJ, EMS, EHJ; end-to-end TPC-H and TPC-DS spilling queries
limitations: Testbed evaluation only; no production deployment data; RDMA backend (Infiniswap) shows software overhead and page-granularity mismatch that can diminish raw RDMA advantage; model assumes fixed budget M and does not address dynamic memory redistribution across concurrent queries; RTT parameter tau proportional to BW*RTT must be estimated for deployment
project_relevance: Topic alignment strong (内存语义、DSA卸载: remote memory/disaggregated memory semantics). REMOP addresses memory resource semantics by exposing transfer-round cost structure of remote memory swapping—directly addressing how memory tier changes latency characteristics. Demonstrates端到端收益传导: operator-level microbenchmark gains (48% runtime reduction, 97% transfer-round reduction) propagate to TPC-H (22.7%) and TPC-DS (26.4%) query-level improvements. No DSA/IAA offload focus, but quantifies CPU/data-movement cost of remote memory semantics through RTT-dominated cost model.
